subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should `openclaw status --deep` use live gateway memory-runtime health as the source of truth for external memory plugins, or is the current `not checked` behavior sufficient outside `status --all`?
rationale: Current main changed the misleading wording but did not implement the live-runtime health contract requested here; the open fork PR and broader https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 need a maintainer-owned choice about the permanent status boundary.

options.title: Make live gateway health canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the canonical implementation path, require real external-memory proof, and close or replace the stale fork PR.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase and prove both human and JSON `status --deep` against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept current wording
options.body: Declare `not checked` sufficient for normal/deep status, close the stale fork PR, and document that memory detail belongs to `status --all` or `memory status --deep`.

recommendation.title: Make live gateway health canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the canonical implementation path, require real external-memory proof, and close or replace the stale fork PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history on the status memory-runtime boundary and introduced the plugin-runtime route that the remaining decision builds on.
